problem_intro: The stock quote page (packages/mo_get_quote) has the richest content in the app, but it is slow and heavy to use. Measured on a Samsung Galaxy M14 (Android 14, 60 Hz):
problem_points: It takes 1.3–2.5 s to open and about 0.9 s to switch tabs, with a skeleton every time the user returns to Overview.
Scrolling runs at about 37 fps with 12 % janky frames.
With nothing changing on screen, it keeps redrawing, uses about half a CPU core and keeps sending data.
It uses over 1 GB of RAM and grows towards 2 GB as the user moves from stock to stock.
There is no chart on the page; the full chart takes more than 7 s to open the first time.
Offline, it gives no message and can stay on a skeleton; a few paths can crash or freeze a tab.
problem_outro: These come from a small number of causes in the code. This plan fixes the biggest cause behind each factor, with front-end changes only, while keeping today's behaviour and features.

factors.problem: Opening a quote takes 1.3 s on a repeat open and about 2.5 s the first time. The page waits for a chain of calls that run one after another, then loads the Overview sections one by one, and shows a shimmer the whole time, although the stock's name and scrip are already known when the page opens.
factors.title: Loading time (opening a quote)
factors.today: 1,313 ms repeat · 2,459 ms first open · ≈ 18 requests, 16 in series
factors.after: ≈ 400–500 ms repeat · ≤ 700 ms first open · ≤ 4 requests in series

causes.text: Opening calls run one after another: dashboard → getQuote → scrip details → getQuote again
The 8 Overview sections load one by one in a for/await loop, and nothing shows until all are done
The header shows a shimmer until the whole chain finishes, although the name and scrip are already known
Nothing is cached, so reopening the same stock starts cold
Artificial waits (100 ms sleep, 300 / 200 ms debounces) and 3 wasted or duplicate calls

covers: The full open waterfall: header on the first frame, then every section as it arrives
Repeat opens served from a short-lived cache
About 4 fewer requests per open, and no 0.00 price flash
not: Nothing major on the FE side; a combined backend endpoint could cut one more round trip later

factors.problem: Switching tabs takes about 0.9 s, and going back to Overview shows a skeleton for about 1.4 s every time. Each switch throws away the data that was already loaded and fetches all of it again.
factors.title: Tab switching
factors.today: 900 ms median · Overview 1.37–1.51 s behind a skeleton every time
factors.after: ≤ 250 ms · no skeleton when revisiting a tab

causes.text: Every switch wipes all three data managers and fetches everything again
The whole content is replaced by a shimmer during the switch
200 ms debounce on every switch
Fundamentals loads its sections one after another

covers: Revisits show the last data at once and refresh in the background
Fundamentals' first load in 2 parallel rounds instead of about 5 serial calls
not: Keeping the tab widget trees alive offstage (D3): large and high risk; D1 + D2 already remove the skeleton and the refetch

factors.problem: Scrolling runs at about 37 fps with 12 % janky frames on a 60 Hz phone. The page does heavy work on every scroll event, builds all 16 Overview sections at once, and rebuilds or repaints far more than what changed.
factors.title: Scrolling and janky frames
factors.today: 37 fps · 11.97 % janky frames · tab-switch frames 40–45 fps

causes.text: On every scroll event the sticky chips walk the whole widget tree, up to 16 times
All 16 Overview sections are built and laid out at once (one shrink-wrapped list inside a SliverToBoxAdapter)
Any accordion tap rebuilds every section; the section list is re-created on every build
A 300 ms programmatic scroll fires in the middle of the user's fling
Custom painters repaint every frame and have no repaint boundaries

covers: Per-scroll UI-thread work removed
Only sections near the viewport are built (lazy slivers)
Rebuilds and repaints limited to what actually changed
No forced jump inside a fling
not: Lighter shadows and blur (B12) and IntrinsicHeight removal (B11): smaller gains, done later

factors.problem: With the market closed and nothing changing on screen, the page still redraws about 13 times a second, uses about half a CPU core and keeps sending data. This drains battery and heats the phone while the user just reads the page.
factors.title: Idle cost (CPU, battery, background data)
factors.today: 13.3 fps of identical frames · 54.3 % CPU · 465 KB/min after market close
factors.after: ≈ 0 fps · ≤ 5 % CPU · much lower background data

causes.text: Two carousels auto-play forever, even off screen, collapsed or in the background
Widgets subscribe to live prices from build() and override each other, re-sending subscribe packets
Collapsed sections stay mounted and rebuild on every tick
Up to four shimmer animations run at once while loading

covers: No animation or rebuild work while nothing changes on screen
Subscribe traffic only on page load or symbol change
not: The single per-page price hub and the mosl_broadcaster unsubscribe API (E1, E5): shared-package work, needed for ≤ 10 KB/min

factors.title: Chart
factors.problem: The quote page has no chart of its own. The only chart is a full-screen WebView that starts cold on the first tap, so the user waits more than 7 s, and the quote page underneath keeps doing tick work while the chart is open.
factors.today: No chart on the quote page · full chart > 7 s on first open · quote page keeps working under the chart
factors.after: WebView start moved off the first chart tap · no tick work under the chart · live price restored on return

causes.text: The WebView and chart path start cold on the first chart tap
The quote page under the chart keeps rebuilding on ticks, and its price can stay frozen after the chart closes

covers: The cold WebView start (about 4 s) happens while the user is still on the quote page, not on the chart tap
The quote page does no work while the chart is on top and resumes its live price on return
not: An inline chart on the quote page (G3): needs a price-history API from the backend
Preloading the chart page and pausing the hidden WebView (G7, G8): high-risk work in the WebView plugin

factors.problem: The quote page uses about 1.1 GB of RAM, mostly graphics, and grows to about 2 GB as the user moves from stock to stock, because old quote pages stay alive underneath.
factors.title: Memory
factors.today: 1,126 MB on the quote page (775 MB graphics) · up to 1,958 MB after ~20 navigations

causes.text: Tapping a peer or last-visited stock stacks a new quote page on top; old pages stay alive with streams and layers
Every section is built and kept in memory at once
Logos decoded at full size; depth handler not disposed

covers: One live quote page at a time, and covered pages paused
Only visible sections hold layers
Smaller images, no leaked depth timers
not: Releasing the chart WebView under memory pressure (F5): shared-package, high risk

factors.problem: When the network drops there is no message, frozen prices look live, the Overview can sit on a skeleton for minutes, and data only comes back about 9 s after the network returns.
factors.title: Offline and reconnect
factors.today: No banner · Overview can stay on a skeleton · ≈ 9 s to recover
factors.after: Banner · no endless skeleton · ≈ 1–2 s to recover

causes.text: About 10 serial calls each wait up to 20 s before giving up
Nothing listens for the network coming back; recovery waits for the socket
No offline banner on the quote page

covers: Offline shows a banner and cached content instead of a skeleton
Failed sections refresh as soon as the network returns
not: An 'as of' time label on frozen prices (H2), left for a later UI pass

factors.problem: A few code paths can crash or leave a tab stuck on a loader: unguarded list access, Errors that 'on Exception' does not catch, emits after the page closes, and a disposed TabController kept by the cubit.
factors.title: Stability

causes.text: Unguarded list access (indexWhere −1, .first on empty, split()[1]) and Errors not caught by 'on Exception'
Emits after the page closes; disposed TabController kept by the cubit

covers: Options and futures tabs never freeze on a loader
No crash on swipe after a segment switch or when leaving during load
not: Section-level errors instead of a full-page error (I8), a larger UI change left for later

phases.title: Phase 1 · Quick wins (low and medium risk, small)
phases.desc: Switch holder first, then the idle, scroll, open and stability fixes that need no structural change.

phases.title: Phase 2 · Loading and tab structure (flagged)
phases.desc: Parallel open and Overview, header from arguments, section cache, keeping tab data. Every change ships behind a switch that keeps today's behaviour when off.

phases.title: Phase 3 · Rendering, memory, chart and offline (flagged)
phases.desc: Lazy slivers, no stacked quote pages, chart warm-up and quote-page pause under the chart, offline banner and reconnect refresh.
